summary: This proposed standard defines the protocol operations of SNMPv2, meaning how its messages are sent and received. It was replaced by RFC 1905.

plainLanguage.summary: This paper lists the actions that managers and devices can perform when they talk to each other, like asking a question or sending an alert.

questions: difference between snmp trap and inform
subtitle: The messages an SNMPv2 manager and agent exchange to read, change and report management information.

tldr.problem: Managers need a defined way to read and change values on network devices, and devices need a way to report problems on their own.
tldr.mechanism: SNMPv2 defines seven PDU types, including Get, GetNext, GetBulk, Set, Response, Inform and Trap, each with precise rules for how the receiver builds its answer.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1448 was a Proposed Standard for SNMPv2 and has been obsoleted by RFC 1905.

today: RFC 1448 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 1905, so it is no longer the current definition of SNMPv2 protocol operations.

sections.title: Roles, Information and Transport
sections.content:
An SNMPv2 entity acts in an agent role when it performs management operations in response to received messages (other than an inform) or sends traps. It acts in a manager role when it starts operations or handles received trap or inform notifications. One entity may do both, and a proxy agent appears to be an agent but satisfies requests by acting as a manager with a remote entity.

A variable is an instance of a non-aggregate object type, and a variable binding pairs a variable's name with its value. The name is an OBJECT IDENTIFIER made of the object type's identifier plus a fragment naming the instance.

Messages need only an unreliable datagram service, with each message entirely contained in one transport datagram. The preferred mapping is the User Datagram Protocol. Whether to retransmit an unanswered request is up to the application, which must act responsibly about frequency and duration.
sections.plainLanguage: Some gadgets ask questions and some answer them, and one gadget can do both. Each question is a short note, and nobody promises the post will always deliver it.

sections.title: PDU Formats and Error Codes
sections.content:
The PDU choices are get-request, get-next-request, get-bulk-request, response, set-request, inform-request and snmpV2-trap. Most share one layout: request-id, error-status, error-index and a variable-bindings list. The GetBulk PDU has the same structure but replaces the two error fields with non-repeaters and max-repetitions.

The request-id in a response copies that of the request, so a manager can match replies to outstanding requests and spot duplicates. Using a different request-id on a retransmission is recommended in most situations so round trip time can be measured.

A non-zero error-status signals a failure, and error-index then points at the failing variable binding, counting from one. The 19 values run from noError(0) and tooBig(1) up to inconsistentName(18). In retrieval, a binding can instead carry the exceptions noSuchObject, noSuchInstance or endOfMibView.
sections.plainLanguage: Every note has a ticket number so replies can be matched to questions. If something goes wrong, the reply says what kind of mistake it was and which question caused it.

sections.title: Reading: Get, GetNext and GetBulk
sections.content:
For a GetRequest, each binding gets the named variable's value. If the object prefix is not found, the value is set to noSuchObject; if only the instance is missing, it is noSuchInstance.

For a GetNextRequest, each binding returns the first lexicographic successor of the requested name. If none exists the value is endOfMibView. Repeating this call walks through a conceptual table.

A GetBulkRequest aims to retrieve large amounts of data in fewer exchanges. The first N bindings (limited by non-repeaters) are handled like GetNext, and each of the remaining R bindings is repeated M times (max-repetitions), so up to N + (M * R) bindings can come back. The response may be shorter if it would exceed the maximum message size. Because very large responses risk IP fragmentation, which the RFC calls generally harmful, only small max-repetitions values should be used under network stress.

If a response would be too big for the requester, the entity sends a tooBig response with an empty binding list instead.
sections.plainLanguage: Get is asking for one specific page. GetNext is asking for the next page after the one you have. GetBulk is asking for a whole stack of pages at once, but not so many that they will not fit in the envelope.

sections.title: Writing and Reporting: Set, Trap and Inform
sections.content:
A SetRequest is processed in two conceptual phases. First every binding is validated and may fail with errors such as noAccess, notWritable, wrongType, wrongValue, inconsistentValue or resourceUnavailable. Only if all pass are the assignments made, as if simultaneously. If one fails, the others are undone and the error is commitFailed; if undo is impossible it is undoFailed. Implementations are strongly encouraged to avoid both.

An agent sends an SNMPv2-Trap-PDU when an exceptional situation occurs. Its first two bindings are sysUpTime.0 and snmpTrapOID.0, followed by any variables in the notification's OBJECTS clause. A trap is unconfirmed: no response is returned.

An InformRequest-PDU goes from one manager to another. The receiver passes its contents to the application and returns a Response-PDU with noError, so it is confirmed.
sections.plainLanguage: Changing a value is all-or-nothing: the gadget checks every change first and only then makes them, so you never end up half changed. A trap is a warning note that needs no answer, while an inform asks the other manager to say it got the message.

sections.title: What Entities Must Support
sections.content:
An agent must be able to generate Response and SNMPv2-Trap PDUs and receive GetRequest, GetNextRequest, GetBulkRequest and SetRequest. A manager must be able to generate Get, GetNext, GetBulk, Set, Inform and Response PDUs and receive Response, SNMPv2-Trap and Inform.

Fields a procedure does not use are ignored, but every part of a PDU must still have valid ASN.1 syntax and encoding. A manager must also be able to handle a response with noSuchName, badValue or readOnly, which exist for proxy compatibility.

The RFC states that security issues are not discussed in this memo.
sections.plainLanguage: There is a checklist of which kinds of notes each side must know how to send and read, so any two devices can understand each other.
